correctness.rationale: In monomial orthonormal coordinates the diagonal of the sampling Gramian is We^{-x}x^k/k!, independent of node angles and positive weights. Minmax comparison gives B/A at least max_k x^k/k! divided by min_k x^k/k!, uniquely minimized where x^n/n!=1. Equality forces the first n nonconstant Fourier moments to vanish; a square angular Vandermonde matrix then forces uniform weights on a rotated regular (n+1)-gon. The Stirling formula has correct leading constant and exponent. This proof is valid for all finite sample counts, including repetitions, and n=1; the accompanying finite spectral checks are corroborative only.
